status: benchmark_contract_authored; no Rust MPS/TEBD backend implemented
claim_ceiling: MPS/TEBD simulation of finite-dimensional U(1)-conserving unitary circuits. This fixture does not qualify Hawking radiation, gravitational backreaction, a Page-island/QES calculation, or a four-dimensional black-hole solution.
motivation: Dense state vectors and dense reduced density matrices are exact but scale exponentially. A scalable programme needs symmetry-preserving tensor networks whose truncation error, bond growth, and output uncertainty are measured rather than hidden.
model_families: nearest-neighbour U(1)-conserving random brickwork circuits from low-entanglement product states
U(1)-conserving sequential product-state boundary emission with immutable emitted factors
operator spreading and squared-commutator profiles when the tensor-network operator backend exists

reference_implementations.name: Quimb CircuitMPS / TEBD
reference_implementations.note: The public documentation exposes explicit maximum bond dimension and cutoff controls; do not compare raw runtime without matched accuracy.

reference_implementations.name: Exact dense Symthaea state-vector backend
reference_implementations.limits: 20-qubit state-vector cap, 64-dimensional retained reduced state cap, dense reference for overlapping small system sizes

reference_implementations.status: to be selected and pinned at implementation time

conventions.symmetry: exact U(1) total excitation number K
conventions.local_gate_family: Haar U(1) x U(2) x U(1) two-site unitaries
conventions.truncation: Schmidt singular values sorted descending; per-bond discarded squared Schmidt weight is recorded before any renormalization
conventions.charge_blocks: each Schmidt block is labeled by its left-block excitation charge q; truncation may not merge distinct q sectors

benchmark_ladder.name: exact-to-MPS overlap
benchmark_ladder.purpose: Compare MPS against the existing exact dense backend on identical fixed gates, initial states, seeds and output checkpoints.
observables: trace distance of reduced density matrices

benchmark_ladder.name: charge-resolved Schmidt truncation accounting
observables: bond dimension by bond and step
benchmark_ladder.negative_control: Truncate across charge sectors or drop an unreported Schmidt tail; the contract must detect it.

benchmark_ladder.name: cost per qualified observable
benchmark_ladder.comparison_rule: Compare dense, MPS and external tensor-network methods at matched state/reduced-state error, same circuit, same seeds, same checkpoint set and same output observables.
benchmark_ladder.prohibited: raw qubits per second or gates per second without an error and truncation receipt

proposed_error_accounting.per_truncation: For a normalized pure state with discarded Schmidt weight delta at one truncation, the distance to its normalized projection is bounded by sqrt(2*delta) in vector 2-norm.
proposed_error_accounting.accumulated: A conservative trajectory envelope is the sum of the per-truncation vector-distance bounds under norm-preserving subsequent unitaries; tighter bounds may be used only with a derivation and matched tests.
proposed_error_accounting.reduced_states: Use contractivity of trace distance under partial trace to propagate the global pure-state error envelope to reduced states.
proposed_error_accounting.entropy: Do not infer a tight entropy error from trace distance alone without dimension-dependent continuity bounds; report the explicit bound or empirical dense overlap.
proposed_error_accounting.caveat: This error accounting is a proposed contract. It does not constitute a proof for an MPS backend that has not been implemented.

negative_controls: discarded Schmidt weight not recorded at each truncation
merge different U(1) charge blocks during truncation
claim an exact result after hitting the bond cap
report entropy without truncation or continuity-error bounds
compare runtime at unequal fidelity or unequal truncation policies
fit diffusion exponents from one system size or post-selected times
interpret MPS circuit dynamics as Hawking radiation or QES physics
